newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dell 96 Europe sales rise 36 percent.
newsitem.headline: Dell 96 Europe sales rise 36 percent.

text.p: Personal computer maker Dell Computer Corp. said on Tuesday a surge led by its German and French units sparked European sales to rise 36 percent to $2 billion in the year ended February 2.
Fourth-quarter European sales surged 34 percent to $618 million as German sales climbed 48 percent and French sales rose 62 percent compared to the year-earlier quarter.
Dell did not break out more specific results by country. Over the past 18 months, the company reorganised its German and French units to focus on large business.
On Tuesday, the U.S. parent company said worldwide sales for the year rose 57 percent to $7.759 billion and net income soared 90 percent to $518 million.
European sales represented 25 percent of Dell's worldwide revenue. The Americas generated 69 percent, or $5.35 billion, while Asia provided six percent, or $465 million.
Rising sales of servers -- high-powered computers that run networks of PCs and control data supplied over the Internet -- and notebook PCs powered Dell's gains, the company said.

In the fourth quarter, worldwide server sales grew more than fourfold compared to the year-ago period, while notebook sales rose 84 percent worldwide, the company said. Desktop PC sales increased 61 percent worldwide during the period.
